reapack.name: StudioSync.lua
reapack.desc: StudioSync: record together remotely over a shared folder

version.author: James
version.changelog: StudioSync: the full rename. The ReaPack package, scripts, actions, repository and installers now carry the new name. If you installed it as BandSync, remove the BandSync repository in ReaPack and add this one.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A new install's ReaPack repository is called StudioSync, and the old name is switched off where it's found.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The nightly backup keeps its folders.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Deleting a copy can't freeze REAPER any more: it goes to the Recycle Bin in the background, with no hidden error box.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Clashes: the owner's change wins, and a Use mine button takes yours back straight from the message. New: colour the whole project, tracks by gradient, folder, instrument, person, newest work and more, and regions by section or along the song.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The classic panel is gone. New mirror tracks say (studio), old (band) ones still count. Several suggestions fold to one line with Review; each says what and how long ago; a grouped fader's suggestion says a folder or VCA goes straight through. Settings Health lists what needs you first, in columns when wide. Restore's filters fold when space is short. Studio cards sit side by side in a wide panel; project rows don't stretch. Driving isn't yellow. A panel failure now names itself in the console.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Track order is the same on every computer: whoever moves a track publishes the list, and each computer comes onto the newest one. A big restore runs in slices so REAPER keeps going, with one undo point. On a Mac, projects reopen at start with no load boxes, using REAPER's own -ignoreerrors (proven on Windows, needs a Mac test).

version.author: James
version.changelog: Produce: a button beside Follow and Listen. Hear someone record on your own grid as it happens, your song a moment behind theirs from your own copy, with Talk between takes; what's being sung over goes quiet here. By default over SonoBus with a position stamp and no server (new effects StudioSync stamp send and read); a NINJAM server is the other route. Colours: items by section, along the song, by person, lane or takes, and a live What's new view that fades over the hour.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Tailscale is back in the installers, not optional: the NINJAM route reaches its server over it. The server's address is saved as this computer's Tailscale name, which doesn't change. Health says if Tailscale isn't installed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: From the first Produce test over real SonoBus: SonoBus joins by itself sooner, a false 'no sound's arriving' warning is gone, the producer's side now hears that someone's recording, and whichever computer has the NINJAM server's folder runs it (in mirrored rooms there's no host).

version.author: James
version.changelog: More from the real Produce test: the stamp reader no longer loses its place when your transport starts, a steady tone can't pass for a stamp at the top of the song, and the NINJAM route cleans up after itself.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The Produce button is on the people cards too, not only the docked list. Stopping the NINJAM route closes ReaNINJAM's window.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Produce through a NINJAM server now tested end to end: a play-through no longer leaves placeholders that play twice on the next pass, and the panel says this route has no talkback.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Docked at the bottom, the panel now looks right both tall and at the mixer's smallest height. Reopening a project no longer sends SWS's recolouring as your edit. Produce through a NINJAM server connects by itself, at the right level, and survives the server going away instead of crashing REAPER. Colouring items counts tracks you made. No more version box on every open.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A backup or autosave of a shared song now asks: open it as a side room you can merge from, or just look. Superior Drummer no longer re-sends the Drums after every playthrough. After a restart, tabs behind the front one sync again. Big projects hitch far less. NINJAM connects by itself on the Play tab and on a Mac, and reconnects if the server drops. Health says whether Tailscale is on.

version.author: James
version.changelog: NINJAM keeps trying for a few minutes when it can't reach the server, and says to press OK if ReaNINJAM shows a box: on a Mac nothing connects until that's pressed.

version.author: James
version.changelog: On a Mac, NINJAM connects once when the server answers, instead of retrying over a connection it can't see.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A shorter line when ReaNINJAM needs its box answered on a Mac.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A real backup file (.rpp-bak) now gets the backup bar; REAPER's offline-when-inactive setting is turned off once; old BandSync actions are removed; the nightly backup skips test songs.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Just look no longer carries over to a new tab of a backup.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The top bar says when the driver's away.

version.author: James
version.changelog: The NINJAM server now ships with StudioSync for Windows and Mac: the first computer to connect runs it, and the next takes over if it's gone. Host it here moves it by hand.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Changing Produce's route takes effect straight away; Bring into main no longer lists deletes of what main already lost.

version.author: James
version.changelog: Whoever's being produced follows the NINJAM server if it moves, and never starts one from an old address.

version.author: James
version.changelog: ReaNINJAM runs out of sight, with its status in the panel (Show it brings its window up). Health says whether Tailscale stays signed in. Produce takes the NINJAM server over if it goes, and everyone follows it if it moves.

version.author: James
version.changelog: A fresh NINJAM connect on a Mac no longer waits on a closed window; the connection box closes as soon as it opens; the route button stays put.
